- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is rising, cap the forecast at 1–2% below the 18-day moving average to prevent false optimism.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot — apply a 3–5 day lagged mean reversion correction to smooth out the peak.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model overfits to recent trends — use a 3-day smoothing filter on forecast to reduce noise.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below forecast, apply a downward bias correction of 2–4% for the next 5 days if sentiment remains neutral or negative.  
- If sentiment is rising steadily, model often overestimates — reduce forecast by 1–3% per 3-day sentiment increase above 0.5.
